PRODUCTS.TITLE: Products
PRODUCTS.DESCRIPTION: Prices and stock the AI agent quotes to customers. These are read from your database exactly, never paraphrased.
PRODUCTS.EMPTY: No products yet. Add the first one above.
PRODUCTS.CONFIRM_DELETE: Delete “{name}”? The agent will stop quoting it.
PRODUCTS.LOAD_ERROR: Could not load products. Check Backend Setup.

POLICIES.TITLE: Policies
POLICIES.DESCRIPTION: Shipping, returns, sizing and warranty. These are indexed for semantic search, so the agent can answer questions phrased any way.
POLICIES.EMPTY: No policies yet. Shipping, returns and sizing are good first ones.
POLICIES.LOAD_ERROR: Could not load policies. Check Backend Setup.

FORM.TITLE: Policy title
FORM.BODY_PLACEHOLDER: Customers may return unworn items within 14 days…
FORM.PUBLISHED: Published — the agent may use this policy

SETTINGS.TITLE: Backend Setup
SETTINGS.DESCRIPTION: Connect Chatwoot to the AI agent backend that stores your catalog and answers customers.
SETTINGS.BACKEND_HELP: Where products and policies are stored. This is your own FastAPI service, not Chatwoot.
SETTINGS.INBOX_HELP: One inbox is one store. Products and policies are scoped to it, so two shops on this Chatwoot never see each other's catalog.
SETTINGS.TEST_OK: Connected — token accepted and catalog readable.
SETTINGS.TEST_TOKEN_NOT_SET: The backend has no KB_ADMIN_TOKEN configured.
SETTINGS.TEST_UNREACHABLE: Backend unreachable. Check the URL, that it is running, and CORS.
SETTINGS.TEST_NOT_CONFIGURED: Enter a backend URL and token first.
SETTINGS.MIXED_CONTENT: Chatwoot is served over HTTPS but this URL is HTTP. Browsers block that as mixed content before CORS is even considered — use an HTTPS URL.
SETTINGS.WEBHOOK_HELP: Chatwoot posts new customer messages here so your agent can reply. This writes a normal Chatwoot webhook — you can see it under Settings → Integrations → Webhooks.
SETTINGS.WEBHOOK_SECRET_TIP: Chatwoot does not sign webhooks, so put a long random secret in the URL path. Generate one with: python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))" — avoid base64, a “/” in the secret splits the path and returns 404.
SETTINGS.PER_USER_NOTE: Note: these settings are stored per user. Another agent signing in will need to enter them again.
